question: A grant writer wants every draft in a project written from the point of view of a programme officer assessing applications, so that weak arguments surface early. What is the best way to set this up?
options: A) Upload sample funded applications to project knowledge and expect Claude to adopt a reviewer stance.
B) Name the perspective in the project title, since the title is what Claude reads first in each new chat.
C) Mention the reviewer's stance in whichever chats feel relevant, so the writer keeps control of when it applies.
D) State the perspective and its purpose in the project instructions so every chat adopts that stance.
correct_answers: D) State the perspective and its purpose in the project instructions so every chat adopts that stance.
explanations: Examples of successful applications do not communicate an assessing point of view.
A project title is a label; it is not where behavioural direction is configured.
This makes an intended default optional and easy to forget on the drafts that need it most.
Correct. A durable stance that should hold for all work in the workspace belongs in project instructions.
